stewardship.content:
# Stewardship of mibz2's production code and releases

This document records who looks after mibz2's production code and releases, what that role
may do without asking, and how a release is carried out and checked. It holds across research
campaigns: a campaign may fail, succeed and finish, or move on to other research, and this
role continues either way. Each campaign keeps its own rules in its own entry document.

## The decision

On 2026-11-04 the maintainer was asked whether the Coordinator's merge and release authority
should be permanent or end with the compact30 campaign. They chose:

> **Permanent steward.** I'm mibz2's standing production and release steward, and compact30 is
> the current campaign under that. A failed experiment stays out of production. A qualified
> improvement doesn't wait indefinitely after passing its gates. Other legitimate maintenance
> isn't held back because of compact30.

The steward is the Coordinator, which is the maintainer's Claude Code session. The role
extended the delegation in the compact30 research charter (§2, report 266) beyond that campaign.
compact30 ended on 2026-11-06. The agent team's standing rules are now `docs/team/RULES.md`
(row A6 is this role).

## The standing objective

The objective is a measurably faster, correct production decoder, properly released. The
steward:
- keeps a failed or unqualified experiment out of production;
- doesn't let a qualified, merged improvement sit unreleased indefinitely;
- doesn't hold other legitimate maintenance back because of a campaign.

## What the steward may do without asking

The steward may open, review and merge pull requests into `master`, and may release, under
these gates.

**Changes that touch measured code** (`src/**`, `Cargo.toml`, `Cargo.lock`, the bench's inputs)
merge only when all of these hold:
- the tests and parity checks pass;
- CI is green on the head that will merge;
- the CI paired A/B bench (`.github/workflows/bench.yml`) shows an end-to-end improvement
  beyond noise, meaning its 95% interval excludes zero in the beneficial direction;
- no other figure regresses unacceptably.

**Target-gated changes** (D071, D072). This route applies only to registrations frozen after
the authorised effective commit that merges this paragraph, citing it, and before any of their
qualification observations. Old data may inform their design but never qualifies. A change to
measured code whose new behaviour is selected only by a *target predicate*, a pure function of
discovered machine facts and the requested thread count, may merge by this route instead of
the beneficial CI interval above. This route is not evidence-equivalent to a CI gain: it
accepts an off-target noninferiority margin of 2%, assessed by the confidence bounds below, in
exchange for on-target superiority under this route. Every condition must be met; missing or
invalid evidence fails.

1. **The predicate is frozen before data,** with its hardware rationale: which discovered facts
   it reads, why each is needed, and how an unknown or unreadable fact is handled (it must
   select the existing plan). A CI test evaluates it on every CI runner and finds it false,
   and asserts that the public dispatch there builds master's plan. Equal plans establish
   fallback selection only, not zero discovery, layout or shared-code cost; that cost is what
   condition 2 bounds.
2. **Off-target noninferiority, on CI.** On the CI paired A/B bench, at every cell of the
   standing CI end-to-end bench at the pinned bench revision (runner configuration × corpus ×
   thread count × wall and CPU time), enumerated completely in the registration, the one-sided
   95% upper bound of head over base is at most 1.02. Every cell must pass: an
   intersection-union test at level 5% for the claim "no cell is worse by more than the
   margin". It is not simultaneous interval coverage, and it does not protect against
   retries; there are none (condition 6). Any omission or change to that standing grid is a
   separate prospective bench-policy decision, not an exclusion available within this route.
   Ratios are head/base times under the registered paired geometric-mean estimator. Passing
   supplies a confidence-based noninferiority conclusion on these cells, not a deterministic
   bound on every machine or run.
3. **On-target superiority, registered before data.** A frozen workstation A/B (RULES C5) on
   a machine where the predicate is true measures the exact candidate against master through
   the public entry point. Every cell in the complete registered on-target machine × workload
   × enabled-budget matrix must pass both tests: wall speed (base/head) lower bound >1.02 and
   CPU time (head/base) upper bound ≤1.02. Let N be the number of required cells and K=2N the
   number of intervals. Use a two-sided wall interval of confidence 1−0.05/K and a one-sided
   CPU upper bound of confidence 1−0.05/K for each cell. These K intervals form one Bonferroni
   family with coverage at least 95%, assuming each constituent interval has its stated
   coverage. Missing, invalid or nonpassing cells fail qualification; no cell may be selected
   or removed after its results.
4. **On-target no harm at the fallback budgets.** In the same run, at every registered
   fallback budget where the predicate is false, wall head over base has a one-sided upper
   bound at most 1.02, Bonferroni over all required fallback machine × workload × budget
   wall-time contrasts: with M such contrasts, each one-sided upper bound has confidence
   1−0.05/M. The registration fixes a nonempty set covering the relevant predicate transitions
   and gives the rationale for any untested fallback budgets. Every one must be shown. NOT
   SHOWN fails qualification; it is not demonstrated harm.
5. **Coverage and adoption reach.** Before qualification data, the registration defines the
   deployment class, the complete required machine × workload × enabled-budget matrix, and the
   measured facts on which its selection depends. Every required cell must qualify. For every
   unmeasured part of that deployment class, it states the mechanism-based grounds for
   extrapolation, the material differences not covered and the residual risk accepted by the
   authorised adoption decision. The coverage requirement and extrapolation are reviewed
   before the qualification run. A narrowed predicate qualifies only to the extent its
   resulting class is covered by this argument; shared facts alone do not establish coverage.
   Where the multi-model route is used, at least two distinct models are required, but model
   count alone is insufficient. If coverage cannot be justified, narrow deployment or obtain
   the missing evidence. Release notes disclose measured scope and extrapolation separately.
6. **The protocol is fixed in the registration:** rounds, the stopping rule (one attempt per
   registration), what makes a run invalid, and what follows an invalid run. No retry to
   pass. A later registration for the same change discloses every earlier attempt and its
   outcome and justifies its information value; all outcomes are retained. Freeze the
   candidate and master baseline commits, public entry point, toolchain and measured inputs,
   pair construction and geometric-mean estimand, interval calculation, complete matrices,
   sample size and stopping rule, exclusions, and invalid-run disposition before any
   qualifying observations, including CI. A changed measured candidate or baseline requires
   fresh evidence under a prospectively justified registration. An invalid attempt is
   retained and never an implicit licence to retry. Later registrations cannot reset the
   no-retry-to-pass rule.
7. **Tests, parity and green CI** hold on the head that merges, and the remaining conditions
   above (no other figure regressing unacceptably) apply as for any measured change. Their
   unacceptable-regression criteria, including the reporting and disposition of CPU and peak
   RSS, are fixed before qualification data, not chosen afterwards.

**Before opening a PR that changes the default decoding kernel,** account for the whole decoder,
not only the part being optimised (RULES.md C4, S2).
- **Count the instructions** executed in `decode_block` on master and on the candidate, split
  into build, walk and the rest. Use matched toolchain, flags and input, and archive the
  profiles. Charge every induced cost: work, memory traffic, synchronisation and control.
- **An excess over master's count needs a stated mechanism,** written down first: what it
  buys (overlap, locality, less contention), its predicted effect at each thread count CI
  measures, and what falsifies it. Falsified, the PR is closed and written up.
- **End-to-end evidence under the applicable acceptance route above decides the merge,** not
  the instruction count alone. The target-gated route requires both its CI and workstation
  conditions.
- **Timing on the shared development machine** is never the evidence. A workstation run is
  evidence only under RULES.md C5.

PR #155 is why: its constructor saved 19.5% of its instructions, its walk added 31%, and CI
measured the decoder 7–19% slower.

**Docs-only and measurement-only changes** merge when CI is green and nothing measured
changed that wasn't meant to.

**A red check** is handled by `docs/team/CI-INCIDENTS.md`. It classifies the failure from its
log, re-runs only the failed job, paced to the outage, and records which checks did not run. It
does not relax the green-head rule above.

**For every merge:**
- merge only the head that CI measured;
- set `expectedHeadSha` to that head;
- a later commit that changes measured code needs a fresh bench.

## Release checkpoints

When accepted production changes have landed on `master`, the steward owns the release:
- Batch changes at sensible milestones. Don't release every research iteration.
- Never release unqualified experimental work.
- Don't leave accepted production improvements indefinitely unreleased.

The release runs through the repository's existing machinery.

1. **Deploy Release** (`.github/workflows/deploy.yml`) is dispatched by hand on `master` with
   `bump` set to patch, minor or major by semver. It runs `just release`
   (`.just/ship.just`), which:
   - bumps the Python and Rust versions together;
   - updates both lockfiles (`Cargo.lock` and `bench/alternatives/Cargo.lock`);
   - writes the crate's changelog with release-plz;
   - commits `chore(release): bump 🐍 -> vX.Y.Z`;
   - tags `py-X.Y.Z`;
   - pushes both the commit and the tag.
2. **The tag alone does not publish anything.** A tag pushed with the workflow's token starts
   no workflow. Deploy Release therefore starts `CI.yml` on the tag itself, by
   `workflow_dispatch`. Creating the tag is not the same as publishing.
3. **CI publishes:**
   - the wheels to PyPI (the `release` job, `pypi` environment);
   - the crate to crates.io through release-plz with Trusted Publishing (the `crates` job,
     `crates-io` environment).

   release-plz also tags `mibz2-vX.Y.Z` and creates the GitHub release.
4. **Verify completion.** All of these must be true before a release counts as done:
   - the CI run on `py-X.Y.Z` succeeded;
   - PyPI lists `mibz2 X.Y.Z`;
   - crates.io lists `mibz2 X.Y.Z`;
   - the GitHub release exists;
   - `CHANGELOG.md` has the version's entry.

   Record the shipped version and its release commit. If any step fails, find the cause and
   reconcile it. A partial publication must not be left unresolved.
5. **Downstream:** bump wikidata-pq's mibz2 pin in a separate PR. That PR follows wikidata-pq's
   own `CLAUDE.md` and must pass its own bench gate. A mibz2 win does not certify a downstream
   gain. A package release is not permission to publish anything to the Hugging Face Hub.

`.github/workflows/tag.yml` is an alternative, for tagging a commit that already carries the
new version. `just ship-rust-and-python` is the local recipe for the same release.

**Identity.** Deploy Release's release commit is made by the workflow's `github-actions[bot]`
identity, as for every prior release. That is the repository's release mechanism, not an
AI-attributed commit. Every other commit is the maintainer's: Louis Maddox
<louismmx@gmail.com>, with no AI attribution in commits, PR bodies, release notes or
metadata.

## What stays with the maintainer

These decisions still need the maintainer:
- relaxing a gate or an acceptance minimum;
- bench design, standing acceptance and adoption policy follow RULES C6 and its review,
  recording and prospective-application safeguards. Relaxing an already registered rule
  remains governed by RULES C2 and D;
- a run on the i9 or another workstation. The maintainer authorises it by running a recipe
  frozen before the run, and that authorises that run only (RULES.md C5);
- new infrastructure, credentials or spending;
- widening the scope beyond mibz2 and its downstream pin bump.

A campaign's rules can reserve more for the maintainer. They cannot give the steward more than
this document and `docs/team/RULES.md` do without the maintainer's own words.

## Standing prohibitions

The steward never:
- reads from, writes to or calls the Hugging Face Hub;
- adds AI attribution;
- changes the allocator;
- weakens the exact checks;
- polls, or sets up cron jobs;
- force-pushes;
- treats silence as approval;
- merges an unbenched head.

## Campaigns

Each campaign has an entry document that maps its charter, roles, protocol, state and evidence.
Read it at the start of a session, after context compaction, and before any consequential
decision. Resolve it to a commit and record the revision that a decision used.

| Campaign | Entry document |
| --- | --- |
| compact30 (ended 2026-11-06, archived) | `docs/journal/compact30-channel/CAMPAIGN.md` (history: `docs/journal/2026-11-06-team-neutral.md`) |

There is no current campaign. The agent team's standing work runs under `docs/team/`.

record.content:
# Decision record (DRAFT, not enacted): the target-gated acceptance route

**Status:** draft, for review. Enacting it needs two things:
- the role tasks' authenticated re-pin to a commit that holds the amended RULES C6 (request 6745788393);
- the Guardian's review of this record and of `docs/STEWARDSHIP.md`'s "Target-gated changes" paragraph (D071, D072), followed by a LOG on #145.

It applies forward only, from the commit that merges it.

**What it decides:** a second, prospective merge route for changes to measured code whose new behaviour only a target predicate selects, and which CI never satisfies. The route is defined in `docs/STEWARDSHIP.md`, conditions 1 to 7.

**Why a route is needed at all.** The standing rule needs a beneficial CI end-to-end interval. A change that switches on only on machines CI doesn't have can never meet it, however it performs on its target. Without a route, every such change is unmergeable by construction. The route doesn't weaken the evidence asked of the target. It asks for superiority there, with a Bonferroni family over the cells, plus no harm at the fallback budgets. What it relaxes is CI's beneficial interval: in its place, CI must show noninferiority within a 2% margin, and nothing more.

## Why 2%

- **It is the margin already in use.** The registrations' no-harm rule uses the same one-sided bound, at most 1.02: the pipelined default's precedent, and the guarded service default's 11 to 20 thread budgets. The route invents no new tolerance.
- **It sits at the CI bench's resolution.** The paired bench's end-to-end intervals at the PR tier are typically about ±1 to 2%. A tighter margin would fail changes that have no real effect, through noise alone. A looser one would admit regressions the bench can resolve.
- **It is a statistical margin, not a guarantee.** Passing shows, with 95% confidence per cell, that no standing CI cell is worse by more than 2% under the registered estimator. It doesn't bound every run or every untested machine.

## Accumulated regressions

A 2% margin against each change's immediate parent is not a lifetime bound. Ten genuine 1% slowdowns, each admitted against its own parent, compound to 1.01^10 ≈ 1.105. So:

- **A drift check at every release.** The release runbook's paired run of the last tag against master (RELEASING.md §3, item 2) is read, for every release that contains a change admitted by this route, as an off-target drift check against the last release. That is a fixed anchor, not the immediate parent.
- **What follows a regression there.** If any standing CI cell shows head over base with a one-sided 95% upper bound above 1.02 against the last release, two things follow:
  - the release notes state it;
  - the route is suspended for new merges until a reviewed decision record either attributes the regression and accepts it explicitly, or reverts the cause.
- **Nothing is netted off.** The check doesn't subtract any target benefit from off-target cost. No fleet-wide gain is inferred from unweighted cells.
- **No lifetime budget beyond the per-release anchor** is set here. A tighter cumulative budget would be its own prospective decision.

## Scope

- **#302 is unaffected.** Its existing result, service-guarded/20261109T195345Z, can't qualify. Its verdict, including NOT SHOWN at 12 and 16, is unchanged. Adopting #302 by this route would need a new registration, frozen after the enacting commit, that meets conditions 1 to 7 and discloses the earlier attempt.
- **Nothing here authorises a run, a merge or a release.**

runbook.content:
# Releasing mibz2

The release runbook. The coordinator follows it step by step for every release. It is
referenced from `CLAUDE.md`, so every session reads it before releasing.

The maintainer's standing instruction is that the coordinator releases mibz2 itself, without
asking first, whenever merged work is worth releasing. Nobody needs to prompt it.

## 1. Is there something worth releasing?

After every merge to master, not only when asked, look at what has merged since the last tag:

```sh
git log <last tag>..master -- src Cargo.toml
```

Worth releasing:
- **A performance gain** shown under its PR's registered rule: the CI bench, or a registered
  workstation run admitted under RULES C5.
- **A change that is definitely committed to:** a fix users need, or an API or packaging
  change.

Docs, journal, bench-harness or blog changes alone are not.

## 2. When

- **Release while the maintainer is around,** not overnight or when they are away from the keyboard. A broken
  release needs someone to hear of it.
- **If work becomes releasable while they are away,** release it when they are next around, and say so.

## 3. Before

1. **Master is green:** Test, Fingerprint and the site.
2. **One paired bench run of the last tag against master:** a `workflow_dispatch` of the Benchmark
   workflow on master, with `base=<the last tag's commit SHA>`. Give it the SHA, never the
   tag name.
   - It checks that nothing got worse. It is not a gate to re-run until the result looks good.
   - Name its CPU. It is in the run's `env.json` artifact and in its step summary.

## 4. The release

1. **Dispatch Deploy Release** with `bump`: patch, or minor for a public API change. It bumps the crate
   and the Python package together, tags `vX.Y.Z` and `py-X.Y.Z`, and starts CI.yml. CI.yml
   publishes the crate (release-plz, Trusted Publishing) and the PyPI wheels.
2. **Verify the publication:**
   - crates.io and PyPI are at the new version, with every wheel and the sdist;
   - docs.rs has built it.
3. **Fix any publishing failure** with a follow-up patch release, as #209 did.

## 5. Release scaling: the new release against the last, on the workstation

The History page's Release scaling view shows each release against the one before it on a
real many-core machine (`bench/release-scaling/`, `docs/generated/release-scaling.md`). It
shows what CI's 4-CPU runners can't, such as the decoder's knee past 8 threads (the
three-team policy came from it). Every release gets one.

1. **As soon as the tag exists, ask Louis to run, on the i9:**

   ```sh
   cd ~/dev/mibz2 && git checkout master && git pull
   just submit bench-release-scaling
   ```

   - With no arguments, the recipe compares the current release (the newest `vX.Y.Z` tag)
     against the last one (the tag before it). Never write version numbers into the command.
   - It is his run, under RULES C5. The agents never time on the workstation. Its figures inform; they don't decide.
2. **When the submission lands on #145:**
   - fetch the bundle from the `evidence` branch at the commit the post names, and check its SHA-256;
   - copy its `recorded/` directory to `bench/release-scaling/<date>-<machine>-<release>/`;
   - commit that to master. The site rebuilds the History page from it.
3. **If the run can't be had** (the i9 is away, or Louis declines), say so in the report. The release
   doesn't wait for it.

## 6. After

1. **A CHANGELOG PR** with the release's notes. #210 is the model. It gives:
   - what changed;
   - the paired run's table and its CPU;
   - the stages;
   - the cost;
   - the caveats;
   - the release-scaling figures once they are in.
2. **The downstream bump:** mibz2 in lmmx/wikidata-pq's `reshape/Cargo.toml`, in a PR. It merges
   under that repository's bench rules.
3. **Report the release:**
   - to the maintainer, in one short message;
   - in the channel log, as a LOG on #145;
   - to the Observer, as a CHECKPOINT.

workflow.content:
# The decoder benchmark: a small, fixed workload decoded in interleaved rounds on one
# runner, by examples/ab.rs (`ab run`), and its figures (bench/report.py).
#
# - A pull request: its head against its base (the merge base with master), both built
#   here and run as two arms of one harness (`mibz2` and `mibz2@base/ab`, the base's own
#   harness binary), so the builds run in the same process shape, their order alternating
#   round to round. The figures go to one comment on the pull request, edited in place.
#   Nothing from a pull request is recorded.
# - A push to master: the commit's mibz2 against the alternatives (pbz2, the lbzip2 CLI,
#   indexed_bzip2, fbz, the lbzip2 crate, libbzip2, libbz2-rs, bz2ngrs and bz2-ng's C),
#   and its inverse BWT against bz2ngrs's and libsais's, its result kept on the
#   bench-results branch (a data-only branch, never merged; nothing is committed to
#   master). The site's benchmark pages are built from it.
# - From the Actions tab: any ref, against the alternatives as on master, or against
#   `base` if given (as on a pull request). Its figures are the run's summary and
#   artifact, never recorded.
#
# The alternatives that are Rust crates with dependencies of their own (fbz, the lbzip2
# crate, libbz2-rs, bz2ngrs) are arms of bench/alternatives' build of the harness
# (`ARM@alts/ab`); indexed_bzip2 runs through Python (bench/ib.py, AB_PYTHON), and bz2-ng's
# C as its own `bzip2 -dc`, built here at a pinned commit (AB_BZ2NG). Single-threaded
# decoders (libbzip2, libbz2-rs, bz2ngrs, bz2ng) run at 1 thread only (examples/ab.rs:
# `parallel`).
#
# The workload: the crate's corpora (`ab gen`, tests/common/mod.rs) at a small scale, and
# 12 MB of the Wikidata dump's own bzip2 blocks (bench/wikidata.json: byte-range windows
# of a dated dump, each window's SHA-256 and the corpus's pinned). At 1 thread, at 2 (one
# CPU on each of 2 cores, `--spread`: the runners' 4 CPUs are 2 cores) and at the runner's
# CPUs, ROUNDS rounds. The 2-thread runs (about 40 s of the run) give CPU amplification
# free of SMT: the report's resources table and its assessment (bench/report.py).
#
# The stages (bench/stages.py): each build's examples/phases.rs on the Wikidata blocks,
# pinned to one CPU, STAGE_ROUNDS rounds of each build once, each stage's fastest of
# STAGE_REPEATS passes of the file in decode order; a
# table of each stage's cycles a byte (head over base on a pull request), beside the
# decoder's figures, not part of them.
name: Benchmark

on:
  pull_request:
    types: [opened, synchronize, reopened, ready_for_review]
    paths:
      - "src/**"
      - "Cargo.toml"
      - "Cargo.lock"
      - "examples/ab.rs"
      - "examples/windows.rs"
      - "examples/phases.rs"
      - "tests/common/**" # (the corpora's recipe)
      - "bench/**"
      - ".github/workflows/bench.yml"
  push:
    branches: [master]
    paths:
      - "src/**"
      - "Cargo.toml"
      - "Cargo.lock"
      - "examples/ab.rs"
      - "examples/windows.rs"
      - "examples/phases.rs"
      - "tests/common/**"
      - "bench/**"
      - ".github/workflows/bench.yml"
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      base:
        description: "A commit to compare against, as on a pull request (empty: mibz2 against the alternatives, as on master)"
        required: false
      base_sample_ms:
        description: "The base arm's thread sampler interval (AB_SAMPLE_MS; 0: none). With base set to the head commit, this measures the sampler's own cost to the decode"
        required: false

# A push to a pull request cancels its run in progress; master's runs each make a record
concurrency:
  group: bench-${{ github.event.pull_request.number || github.sha }}-${{ inputs.base }}
  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}

permissions:
  contents: write # (master: the bench-results and bench-data branches)
  pull-requests: write # (the comment)

env:
  ROUNDS: 10
  SCALE: 4 # ab gen's: corpora of 8-20 MB of output each
  SETTLE: 0.25 # seconds the harness samples the other processes' load before each run
  STAGE_ROUNDS: 5 # bench/stages.py's rounds (each 13-17 s on the runners seen)
  STAGE_REPEATS: 2 # phases' passes a run, each a decode of the file (each stage's fastest kept)
  KERNEL_PASSES: 10 # bench/alternatives' kernels: passes of both inverse BWTs over the Wikidata blocks (about 3 s each)
  RUN_URL: ${{ github.server_url }}/${{ github.repository }}/actions/runs/${{ github.run_id }}
  CARGO_TERM_COLOR: never

jobs:
  bench:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 60
    steps:
      # A pull request's head commit itself, not GitHub's merge of it into the base
      - uses: actions/checkout@v6
        with:
          ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha || github.sha }}
          fetch-depth: 0

      - name: Arms
        env:
          PR_HEAD: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
          PR_BASE: ${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha }}
          INPUT_BASE: ${{ inputs.base }}
        run: |
          head=$(git rev-parse HEAD)
          case "$GITHUB_EVENT_NAME" in
            pull_request) mode=pr; base=$(git merge-base "$PR_BASE" "$PR_HEAD") ;;
            push) mode=master; base= ;;
            *) if [ -n "$INPUT_BASE" ]; then mode=pr; base=$(git rev-parse "$INPUT_BASE^{commit}"); else mode=dispatch; base=; fi ;;
          esac
          if [ "$mode" = pr ]; then
            arms="mibz2,mibz2@base/ab"
          else
            arms="mibz2,pbz2,lbzip2,indexed_bzip2,fbz@alts/ab,lbzip2-rs@alts/ab,libbzip2,libbz2-rs@alts/ab,bz2ngrs@alts/ab,bz2ng"
          fi
          {
            echo "MODE=$mode"; echo "HEAD_SHA=$head"; echo "BASE_SHA=$base"; echo "ARMS=$arms"
            echo "HEAD_DATE=$(git show -s --format=%cI "$head")"
          } >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
          echo "mode $mode, head $head, base ${base:-none}, arms $arms"

      - name: Comment (pending)
        if: github.event_name == 'pull_request'
        continue-on-error: true # (a fork's pull request has a read-only token)
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: python3 bench/comment.py pending ${{ github.event.pull_request.number }} "$HEAD_SHA"

      # lbzip2: an arm, and examples/windows.rs's check of the Wikidata blocks
      - name: lbzip2
        run: sudo apt-get install -y -qq lbzip2 > /dev/null && lbzip2 --version | head -1

      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable
      - uses: Swatinem/rust-cache@v2

      # The release profile (Cargo.toml's: fat LTO, one codegen unit), as published
      - name: Build the head
        run: |
          cargo build --release --example ab --example windows --example phases
          mkdir -p bin && cp target/release/examples/ab bin/ab && cp target/release/examples/phases bin/phases

      # The alternatives (master and the Actions tab only): bench/alternatives' build of the
      # harness, and indexed_bzip2 in a virtualenv of its own
      - name: Build the alternatives
        if: env.MODE != 'pr'
        run: |
          # libsais 2.12.1 at a pinned commit, single-threaded, for the kernels binary's libsais
          # kernel (bench/libsais.sh: its source checked by SHA-256)
          # (two steps, so a failed build fails the step: `export` would hide its status)
          LIBSAIS_DIR=$(bash bench/libsais.sh "$RUNNER_TEMP/libsais")
          export LIBSAIS_DIR
          CARGO_TARGET_DIR="$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/target/alts" cargo build --release --locked --manifest-path bench/alternatives/Cargo.toml
          mkdir -p alts && cp target/alts/release/ab target/alts/release/kernels alts/
          # bz2-ng's C at a pinned commit, its CLI (CMake's Release build, as its README builds it)
          ng=517948ed836d4c52d68d8e633887aaa21c17ba27
          git init -q "$RUNNER_TEMP/bz2-ng" && git -C "$RUNNER_TEMP/bz2-ng" fetch -q --depth 1 https://github.com/tfenne/bz2-ng "$ng"
          git -C "$RUNNER_TEMP/bz2-ng" checkout -q FETCH_HEAD
          cmake -S "$RUNNER_TEMP/bz2-ng/c" -B "$RUNNER_TEMP/bz2-ng/build" -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release -DBZ2NG_BUILD_SHARED=OFF \
            -DBZ2NG_BUILD_TESTS=OFF -DBZ2NG_BUILD_BENCH=OFF -DBZ2NG_BUILD_FUZZ=OFF > /dev/null
          cmake --build "$RUNNER_TEMP/bz2-ng/build" -j "$(nproc)" --target bzip2 > /dev/null
          echo "AB_BZ2NG=$RUNNER_TEMP/bz2-ng/build/bzip2" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
          python3 -m venv "$RUNNER_TEMP/ib" && "$RUNNER_TEMP/ib/bin/pip" install -q indexed_bzip2==1.7.0
          echo "AB_PYTHON=$RUNNER_TEMP/ib/bin/python" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"

      - name: Build the base
        if: env.MODE == 'pr'
        env:
          BASE_SAMPLE_MS: ${{ inputs.base_sample_ms }}
        run: |
          git worktree add --detach .base-src "$BASE_SHA"
          test -f .base-src/examples/ab.rs || { echo "::error::the base $BASE_SHA has no examples/ab.rs"; exit 1; }
          # (and its examples/phases.rs, for the stage table, where it has one)
          phases=$(test -f .base-src/examples/phases.rs && echo "--example phases" || true)
          (cd .base-src && CARGO_TARGET_DIR="$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/target" cargo build --release --example ab $phases)
          mkdir -p base && cp target/release/examples/ab base/ab
          if [ -n "$phases" ]; then cp target/release/examples/phases base/phases; fi
          # (the Actions tab only: the base arm with its own sampler interval, AB_SAMPLE_MS)
          if [ -n "$BASE_SAMPLE_MS" ]; then
            mv base/ab base/ab-bin
            printf '#!/bin/sh\nAB_SAMPLE_MS=%s exec "%s" "$@"\n' "$BASE_SAMPLE_MS" "$PWD/base/ab-bin" > base/ab
            chmod +x base/ab
            echo "base arm: AB_SAMPLE_MS=$BASE_SAMPLE_MS"
          fi

      - name: Corpora
        run: bin/ab gen corpora "$SCALE"

      # Wikimedia serves a dated dump for about six weeks: the windows are kept on the
      # bench-data branch once a master run has read them, and read from there first
      - name: Wikidata windows (cache)
        uses: actions/cache@v4
        with:
          path: windows
          key: bench-wikidata-${{ hashFiles('bench/wikidata.json') }}

      - name: Wikidata windows
        run: |
          dir=$(python3 -c 'import json; print(json.load(open("bench/wikidata.json"))["windows_dir"])')
          if [ "$(ls "$dir"/*.bin 2>/dev/null | wc -l)" = 0 ] && git fetch -q origin bench-data:refs/remotes/origin/bench-data 2>/dev/null; then
            git archive origin/bench-data "$dir" | tar -x || true
          fi
          source=$(python3 bench/wikidata.py fetch bench/wikidata.json "$dir")
          echo "WINDOWS_SOURCE=$source" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
          echo "WINDOWS_DIR=$dir" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
          python3 bench/wikidata.py build bench/wikidata.json "$dir" target/release/examples/windows corpora/wikidata.bz2
          ls -l corpora

      # The runner as the runs see it (cores, quota, the run-queue counter's check)
      - name: Environment
        run: bin/ab env | tee env.json

      - name: Run
        run: |
          threads=$([ "$(nproc)" -gt 2 ] && echo "1,2,$(nproc)" || echo "1,$(nproc)")
          bin/ab run runs.jsonl --arms "$ARMS" --threads "$threads" --spread --rounds "$ROUNDS" --settle "$SETTLE" corpora/*.bz2

      # Each stage on its own, on one thread: a diagnostic beside the decoder's figures
      - name: Stages
        run: |
          if [ "$MODE" = pr ]; then
            arms="head=bin/phases"; [ -x base/phases ] && arms="base=base/phases $arms"
          else
            arms="mibz2=bin/phases"
          fi
          start=$SECONDS
          python3 bench/stages.py run stages.jsonl --rounds "$STAGE_ROUNDS" --repeats "$STAGE_REPEATS" corpora/wikidata.bz2 $arms
          echo "stages: $((SECONDS - start)) s"

      # The inverse BWT alone, mibz2's against bz2ngrs's phase by phase, on one CPU (master
      # and the Actions tab only: bench/alternatives' kernels binary)
      - name: Kernels
        if: env.MODE != 'pr'
        run: |
          start=$SECONDS
          taskset -c 1 alts/kernels corpora/wikidata.bz2 "$KERNEL_PASSES" kernels.jsonl
          echo "kernels: $((SECONDS - start)) s"

      # the report's stage table across builds whose phases report different stages
      - name: Report tests
        run: python3 bench/test_report.py

      - name: Figures
        run: |
          ref=$([ "$MODE" = pr ] && echo "mibz2@base/ab" || echo mibz2)
          { echo "## ab summary (reference: $ref)"; bin/ab summary runs.jsonl --ref "$ref"; } > ab-summary.md
          python3 bench/report.py summary runs.jsonl --corpora corpora --mode "$MODE" --head "$HEAD_SHA" \
            ${BASE_SHA:+--base "$BASE_SHA"} --date "$HEAD_DATE" --run "$RUN_URL" --stages stages.jsonl --env env.json --kernels kernels.jsonl \
            --out result.json --md comment.md
          cat comment.md ab-summary.md >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          # (the resources section in the log too, where a dispatched run's figures can be read)
          sed -n '/^### Resources/,/^<\/details>/p' comment.md

      - name: Comment
        if: "!cancelled() && github.event_name == 'pull_request'"
        continue-on-error: true
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          if [ -f comment.md ]; then
            python3 bench/comment.py final ${{ github.event.pull_request.number }} comment.md
          else
            python3 bench/comment.py failed ${{ github.event.pull_request.number }} "$HEAD_SHA"
          fi

      - name: Results
        if: "!cancelled()"
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: bench-${{ env.MODE }}-${{ env.HEAD_SHA }}
          path: |
            runs.jsonl
            env.json
            stages.jsonl
            kernels.jsonl
            result.json
            comment.md
            ab-summary.md
          if-no-files-found: ignore

      # master only: the commit's result appended to the bench-results branch, and the
      # Wikidata windows kept on the bench-data branch if they were read from Wikimedia
      - name: Record
        if: success() && github.event_name == 'push' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/master'
        run: |
          git config user.name "github-actions[bot]"
          git config user.email "41898282+github-actions[bot]@users.noreply.github.com"
          # (a data-only branch, checked out beside the code: its last commit, or a new one)
          open_branch() {
            if git fetch -q origin "$1:refs/remotes/origin/$1" 2>/dev/null; then
              git worktree add -q --detach "$2" "origin/$1"
            else
              git worktree add -q --orphan -b "$1" "$2"
            fi
          }
          push_branch() {
            for try in 1 2 3; do
              git -C "$2" push -q origin "HEAD:$1" && return 0
              git -C "$2" fetch -q origin "$1" && git -C "$2" rebase -q FETCH_HEAD
            done
            return 1
          }
          open_branch bench-results .store
          python3 bench/report.py record .store result.json runs.jsonl
          git -C .store add -A
          git -C .store commit -qm "record bench: ${HEAD_SHA::7}, bench $(python3 -c 'import json; print(json.load(open("result.json"))["bench"])')"
          push_branch bench-results .store
          if [ "$WINDOWS_SOURCE" != kept ] || ! git cat-file -e "origin/bench-data:$WINDOWS_DIR" 2>/dev/null; then
            open_branch bench-data .data
            mkdir -p ".data/$WINDOWS_DIR" && cp "$WINDOWS_DIR"/*.bin ".data/$WINDOWS_DIR/" && cp bench/wikidata.json ".data/$WINDOWS_DIR/"
            python3 bench/wikidata.py readme bench/wikidata.json > .data/README.md
            git -C .data add -A
            if git -C .data diff --cached --quiet; then
              echo "bench-data already holds $WINDOWS_DIR"
            else
              git -C .data commit -qm "bench data: $WINDOWS_DIR"
              push_branch bench-data .data
            fi
          fi

report_ratio_ci:
def ratio_ci(r: list[float]) -> list[float] | None:
    """[geometric mean, low, high] of paired ratios: a t-interval on their logs."""
    r = [x for x in r if x and x > 0 and math.isfinite(x)]
    if len(r) < 2:
        return None
    m, h = mean_ci([math.log(x) for x in r])
    return [round(math.exp(m), 4), round(math.exp(m - h), 4), round(math.exp(m + h), 4)]

+# Decision record (DRAFT, not enacted): the target-gated acceptance route
+
+**Status:** draft, for review. Enacting it needs two things:
+- the role tasks' authenticated re-pin to a commit that holds the amended RULES C6 (request 6745788393);
+- the Guardian's review of this record and of `docs/STEWARDSHIP.md`'s "Target-gated changes" paragraph (D071, D072), followed by a LOG on #145.
+
+It applies forward only, from the commit that merges it.
+
+**What it decides:** a second, prospective merge route for changes to measured code whose new behaviour only a target predicate selects, and which CI never satisfies. The route is defined in `docs/STEWARDSHIP.md`, conditions 1 to 7.
+
+**Why a route is needed at all.** The standing rule needs a beneficial CI end-to-end interval. A change that switches on only on machines CI doesn't have can never meet it, however it performs on its target. Without a route, every such change is unmergeable by construction. The route doesn't weaken the evidence asked of the target. It asks for superiority there, with a Bonferroni family over the cells, plus no harm at the fallback budgets. What it relaxes is CI's beneficial interval: in its place, CI must show noninferiority within a 2% margin, and nothing more.
+
+## Why 2%
+
+- **It is the margin already in use.** The registrations' no-harm rule uses the same one-sided bound, at most 1.02: the pipelined default's precedent, and the guarded service default's 11 to 20 thread budgets. The route invents no new tolerance.
+- **It sits at the CI bench's resolution.** The paired bench's end-to-end intervals at the PR tier are typically about ±1 to 2%. A tighter margin would fail changes that have no real effect, through noise alone. A looser one would admit regressions the bench can resolve.
+- **It is a statistical margin, not a guarantee.** Passing shows, with 95% confidence per cell, that no standing CI cell is worse by more than 2% under the registered estimator. It doesn't bound every run or every untested machine.
+
+## Accumulated regressions
+
+A 2% margin against each change's immediate parent is not a lifetime bound. Ten genuine 1% slowdowns, each admitted against its own parent, compound to 1.01^10 ≈ 1.105. So:
+
+- **A drift check at every release.** The release runbook's paired run of the last tag against master (RELEASING.md §3, item 2) is read, for every release that contains a change admitted by this route, as an off-target drift check against the last release. That is a fixed anchor, not the immediate parent.
+- **What follows a regression there.** If any standing CI cell shows head over base with a one-sided 95% upper bound above 1.02 against the last release, two things follow:
+  - the release notes state it;
+  - the route is suspended for new merges until a reviewed decision record either attributes the regression and accepts it explicitly, or reverts the cause.
+- **Nothing is netted off.** The check doesn't subtract any target benefit from off-target cost. No fleet-wide gain is inferred from unweighted cells.
+- **No lifetime budget beyond the per-release anchor** is set here. A tighter cumulative budget would be its own prospective decision.
+
+## Scope

Adopting #302 by this route would need a new registration, frozen after the enacting commit, that meets conditions 1 to 7 and discloses the earlier attempt.
